results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 60 outline summaries match the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph, in spec order; the three callouts map to no paragraph.
Fraud and Card Data ¶5: Spec p35 declares the script risk and the rule as one causally linked idea (the risk is why the rule exists).
What to Take Away ¶2: Spec p55 is a declared labelled list ('Established') of parallel items: one idea.
What to Take Away ¶3: Spec p56 is a declared labelled list ('Depends on context'): one idea.
What to Take Away ¶4: Spec p26 is a declared labelled list ('Still moving'): one idea.
What to Take Away ¶5: Spec p57 is a declared labelled list ('The author's synthesis'): one idea.
Every unit serves S1-S6 or the introduction/conclusion; no orphan paragraphs.

results.draft_locus: What a Payment Service Provider Does ¶7 (l.86)
results.quote: is capped in the EU at 0.2% for consumer debit and 0.3% for consumer credit cards (Regulation (EU) 2015/751, in force since 9 December 2015)
results.finding: The interchange cap is quoted but never used: the worked €100 illustration computes iDEAL and Klarna but not the card, so the reader cannot see what the cap shows about the fee line. Either compute the card fee from it or drop the sentence. Both flow readers stumbled on this.

results.draft_locus: What a Payment Service Provider Does ¶1 (l.46), after Setting the Scene ¶5
results.quote: When Eva pays, at least five parties take part.
results.finding: Declared elaboration carrying over 'the question of how the order finds out what the PSP did' (Noor's question). The section opens after the Card-Testing Night paragraph with no link to that question or to why the parties matter for answering it; Eva also re-enters without a bridge. Nothing at the boundary expresses the elaboration.

results.quote: The chapter ends with a refund alternative to her later exchange of the jacket for size L.
results.finding: Flow reader A: 'Mentions an exchange not yet told; hard to parse. Also line 20 says the chapter "ends with" the refund variant, line 22 says it "ends with Eva's payment worked through and the ways payment integrations fail" — two different endings.' The exchange is a later event in the book and is not signalled as such, and the two 'ends with' sentences contradict each other.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flowB item 3, l.20 ('Exchange not mentioned; hard to parse; re-read')

results.quote: the days and details are fictional.
results.finding: Flow reader A: 'The whole company is fictional; the hedge raises questions.' The hedge breaks the frame of an already fictional case.
